governing_thought: Physics is divided by the scale of the system studied: subatomic, atomic and optical, condensed and soft matter, plasmas and fluids, and gravitational and cosmic.
dimension: the scale of the system studied
rank_note: Ranked from the smallest systems to the largest; plasmas and fluids are placed by their continuum description.

pillars.title: Subatomic
pillars.statement: The subatomic scale covers elementary particles, quantum fields and atomic nuclei.

pillars.title: Atomic, molecular and optical
pillars.statement: The atomic, molecular and optical scale covers atoms, molecules, light and the quantum probes that resolve them.

pillars.title: Condensed and soft matter
pillars.statement: The condensed and soft matter scale covers many-particle systems: phases, solids, liquids, electronic and magnetic materials, soft, living and network matter.

pillars.title: Plasmas, fluids and continua
pillars.statement: The plasma, fluid and continuum scale covers matter described as a continuous medium: flow, transport, waves, beams and plasmas.

pillars.title: Gravitation and the cosmos
pillars.statement: The gravitational and cosmic scale covers gravity, relativity, stars, galaxies and the universe as a whole.

method_line.title: Method line
method_line.covers: physics teaching, history and general methods

route_note: Routing rules (strict): every solid-earth, seismology, volcanic, seafloor, ocean, atmosphere, geophysics or near-Earth space topic goes in routed (it belongs to earth sciences, EA), never under a pillar. Physics teaching, history and general methods go only in the Method line. Place applied topics by the scale of the system they study: classical mechanics, acoustics and continuum waves under Plasmas, fluids and continua; networks and complex systems under Condensed and soft matter; medical physics goes in routed (medicine, MD) and energy technology in routed (engineering, EN) unless it is clearly about one physical scale. P3 and P4 must not overlap: fluids and continuum flow only in P4, soft and living matter only in P3. No section may be named after or organised by a classification code or scheme. Also: network science and complex-systems topics go in routed (computing, CS); biological physics stays in P3 only if about soft matter, otherwise routed (biology, BI). Classical mechanics must be split by system (continuum and wave items to P4, celestial mechanics to P5); no P4 section may be a generic 'classical physics' bucket. Never use PACS, PhySH or other code entries as section headings; retire only leaf items, never group ids.
